- **Fire Protection Criteria Manual (FPCM):** §§ 4.4.0 (general), 4.7.0 (NFPA 13), 4.8.0 (NFPA 14 / standpipes), 4.9.0 (NFPA 20 / pumps), 4.10.0 (WUI); Appendix E §§ 1.1.0, 2.1.0, 2.4.0, 3.2.x (submittal content).
- **Utilities Criteria Manual (UCM):** § 2.9.2 (water/fire flow); UCM 2.9.2.D.1 (hydrant spacing); UCM 2.9.2.B.6 (fire line material, BFP, flow detection).
- **Standard Specifications Manual (SSM):** Item 511.4.B (hydrant physical placement); Standards 901S-1, 901S-2, 901S-5, 901S-6 (apparatus access, turnarounds, fire-zone signs).
- **Transportation Criteria Manual (TCM):** §§ 7.3, 7.5 (driveways serving fire lanes); ASMP Street Network Map for street-level lookup.
- **Hydrant flow data:** AFD hydrant flow test report (Fire Marshal-witnessed; ≤1 year old). Fire Flow Map "Box" number on AW General Info & Construction Notes Sheet.
- **WUI map:** 2024 WUI Code Map (dark blue/teal = Zones A & B combined; light blue = Zone C). Map does not distinguish A from B — AFD Wildfire Division field-measures.

## Regulatory pathway

Fire review runs **concurrently** with civil/site plan review through Development Services Department, but AFD has independent sign-off authority. Plans with fire lines additionally require both AFD and DSD approval before Austin Water Processing and Evaluation (AWPE) will approve (UCM 2.5.1.D).

- **Pre-application:** AFD pre-app meeting strongly advisable for high-rise, podium, mixed-construction, WUI, alternative-surface fire lanes, or any site requiring an AMOC. AFD will not issue AMOC approval numbers during site plan cycle — AMOC must be a **separate standalone submittal**, approved before site plan submission.
- **AMOC track (IFC § 104.8):** Required when standard IFC requirements cannot be met — most commonly to reduce minimum commercial fire flow below 1,500 gpm (floor: 1,000 gpm), reduce hydrant coverage, or approve pyrophoric gas storage. AMOC must be pre-approved with an AFD-issued approval number and date noted in the AFD Fire Analysis Table. "Pending"/"submitted" entries are deficient.
- **WUI track (FPCM 4.10.0):** Concurrent review by AFD Wildfire Division. Required for any property within Full/Limited Purpose Jurisdiction that the 2024 WUI Code Map covers or that AFD Wildfire designates. Separate WUI approval stamp required before final site plan approval. Map status is rebuttable only by AFD Wildfire Division — self-declared "not in WUI" is a deficiency.
- **High-rise track (IBC § 202 via LDC § 25-12-1):** Any occupied floor >75 ft above the lowest level of fire department vehicle access triggers IBC § 403 high-rise requirements: Fire Command Center (1-hr fire barrier; exterior access or 2-hr rated passageway; FPCM Appendix E § 3.2.13 equipment list), dual remote FDCs (NFPA 14 § 7.12.2), fire pump room, dual water mains (UCM 2.9.2.A.3.e), AEDs each occupied level, simultaneous stairway-unlock controls (LDC § 25-12-173 § 508.1.6). For buildings >420 ft, mains must be in **different streets** (IFC § 914.3.1.2). Buildings between ~65–75 ft must carry three pre-CO survey notes (ZLU-29.10/.11/.12).
- **Decision body:** Fire Marshal's office; Wildfire Division (for WUI); final sign-off on cover sheet approval block.
- **Timeline reality:** AMOC review adds ~6–12 weeks before site plan submission becomes viable. WUI concurrent review rarely controls the critical path. High-rise pre-app + dual-main coordination with Austin Water can add 1–2 cycles. Any post-approval change to fire lanes, hydrants, FDCs, fire service routing, riser/pump rooms, or electric disconnect requires AFD resubmission.

## Constraints to evaluate

**Apparatus access (LDC § 25-12-173 §§ 503.1.1, 503.2.1, 503.2.4 with City amendments; Appendix D not adopted).**
- Fire apparatus access road within **150 ft** (path-of-travel, not arc) of all portions of all exterior walls of the first story. AFD routinely extends to **200 ft** for buildings fully sprinklered per NFPA 13 (not 13R/13D) under Exception 1.1, but the increase is **discretionary** — plans showing 200 ft must reflect AFD authorization; high-piled combustible storage buildings (>12,000 sf area + storage >12 ft height) are locked at 150 ft regardless of sprinklers (IFC § 3206.6). High-piled storage also requires one FD access door per 100 LF of exterior wall facing the access road, max 125 ft center-to-center (IFC § 3206.6.1, § 3206.7.5).
- Measurement: actual ground-level path around obstructions ≥4 ft tall (buildings, walls, fences, grade changes); never through/under buildings; never across water-quality features; AFD will not lay supply hose across ASMP Level 3+ arterials, expressways, parkways, freeways, or toll roads. Routes that cross property lines require a recorded **JUAE or UDA** (§ 503.1.1 Exception 3).
- **Minimum unobstructed width 25 ft** face-of-curb to face-of-curb (sidewalk does not count); 14 ft minimum vertical clearance for the full width; **inside turning radius 25 ft / outside 50 ft** (§ 503.2.4). Wider than 25 ft lanes may reduce to 20-in/40-out. Divided fire lanes where aerial is not anticipated: two 15-ft lanes (Exception 2.d). Security gates: 25 ft two-way / 15 ft one-way (20 ft two-way only with prior Fire Prevention Division written approval). Throat at Level 1/2 street crosswalk: 20 ft permitted (Exception 2.e). Curb-return radii at fire-access driveways from public streets follow TCM 7.5.1.1 Table 7-1 "Fire Access" column — typically 15 ft on Level 1/2 streets (vs. 10 ft typical). Turning movements onto opposing traffic lanes or where ASMP proposes a raised median are prohibited.
- **Grade:** asphalt ≤ 13%; concrete ≤ 15%; maximum 10% change in any 20 ft; aerial setup areas ≤ ~12–13% running and 3.5% cross-slope; driveway grade change in a fire lane ≤ 6% (TCM 7.5.2.1.E, more restrictive). Where max grades cannot be met, a fully protected sprinkler system approved by AFD may substitute. Minimum drainage: 2% vegetated / alternative; 1% asphalt; 0.5% concrete.
- **Surface:** HS-20 loading (16 kips/wheel, 80,000 lbs total) for all fire lanes and all structural elements within them (manhole covers, vault lids, trench grates). Final asphalt/concrete must be in place before combustible construction begins. Alternative surfaces (grasscrete, pavers, PICP, porous asphalt/concrete) limited to ≤25% of building-perimeter fire protection, require slip-resistant surfaces at turns and 40 LF at building corners for aerial operations, reinforced mountable curb when no Type I/II apron is present, and a post-completion PE-of-record concurrence letter (§ 503.2.3.1). Pervious or decorative paving **within 100 ft of any building** requires AFD approval + PE design for 80,000 lb live load even when not formally a fire lane.

**Aerial apparatus (LDC § 25-12-173 § 503.2.6.1; AFD operational practice).**
- Aerial-clearance review begins at ~73 ft per AFD practice (2 ft before the 75-ft high-rise threshold). For high-rise and near-high-rise buildings, plans must demonstrate clear staging adjacent to the building face — typically a 25-ft setback envelope plus overhead clearance for the boom. Divided 15-ft lanes are not permitted where aerial deployment is expected; full 25-ft lane required.
- Elevated surfaces (podium slabs, plaza decks) that serve as fire apparatus access must be designed for the greater of IFC § 503.2.6 apparatus loads or IBC § 1607.8.1 live load (LDC § 25-12-3 § 1607.8.2). **Outrigger loads:** **43,200 lbs on one outrigger** or **28,600 lbs each on two adjacent outriggers** at 18-ft center spacing on 24"×24" contact (§ 503.2.6.1). Engineer of record must sign a post-completion concurrence letter. Access hatches, vault covers, and trench grates in the apparatus path must individually carry the 43,200-lb single-outrigger rating.
- Bridges/elevated fire lane crossings: AASHTO HB-17 (or current LRFD) design; load-limit signs at both entrances (§ 503.2.6).

**Dead-ends and turnarounds.**
- Dead-end fire lane >150 ft requires a turnaround per Standard 901S-2: cul-de-sac with 50-ft unobstructed radius **or** hammerhead/T 25 ft × 80 ft with 10 ft additional clearance and no obstructions over 1 ft (FPCM 4.4.0).
- Turnaround pavement must be marked fire lane on all sides; hose-lay extension from the turnaround counts toward apparatus-to-building distance.

**Hydrant coverage and spacing (LDC § 25-12-173 § 507.5.1; UCM § 2.9.2.D).**
- Primary hydrant hose-lay to all exterior walls: **400 ft** non-sprinklered (non-R-3/U); **500 ft** for buildings sprinklered throughout per NFPA 13 or 13R; **600 ft** for Group R-3 and U regardless of sprinklers.
- **Second hydrant within 500 ft (600 ft for R-3/U) when required fire flow ≥1,500 gpm; additional hydrants within 1,000 ft when fire flow >2,500 gpm. One hydrant per 1,250 gpm (or fraction).** Multi-hydrant calcs must show all required hydrants flowing simultaneously, starting at the most hydraulically remote.
- **Spacing:** **300 ft** maximum interval in commercial/high-density areas (CBD, DMU, W/LO, CS, CH, MF-4/5/6, or inside the Downtown Austin Project Coordination Zone); **600 ft** max interval elsewhere; hydrant at every major intersection; hydrants on **both sides** of any divided road regardless of arterial class (UCM 2.9.2.D.2).
- **Placement (SSM 511.4.B):** 3–6 ft behind curb gutter face; steamer center ≥18 in above grade; steamer perpendicular to and facing the curb/fire lane; ≥20 ft from curb tangency at corners; ≥9 ft (any direction) from sanitary sewer line/lateral/service/manhole (UCM 2.9.2.D.4); ≥5 ft from storm drain; ≥3 ft clear circumference; bollards where exposed to vehicles; lead line ≤55 ft from main and cannot cross a divided road.
- **Field-verified fire flow test:** AFD-conducted or AFD-witnessed only (IFC § 507.4 as locally amended); ≤1 year old at site-plan submission; on hydrants on the same main/zone serving the connection point; full FPCM Appendix E § 2.4.0 data set (static, residual, pitot, flow rate, hydrant IDs, date/time, conductor, equipment, gauge elevations).
- **Required fire flow at 20 psi residual** from IFC Appendix B Table B105.1(2) using IBC construction type + fire-flow calculation area per LDC § 25-12-173 B104.1. Commercial floor: 1,500 gpm (reducible to 1,000 gpm only with pre-approved AMOC). Sprinkler reductions per Table B105.2: NFPA 13 → 75%; NFPA 13R → 50% (capped at 50% for Type III/IV/V); NFPA 13D → 25%. **No reduction** for Group H or S-1/S-2 with high-piled or rack storage.
- Hydraulic calc C-factors are fixed by FPCM 4.4.0 Table 507-2: C=80 (iron/steel) or C=110 (plastic/copper) — software defaults of 140/150 are non-compliant. **Velocity ≤10 fps** upstream of the 6-in hydrant tap; the 6-in lead downstream is the only velocity exception.

**FDC siting (IFC § 912; LDC § 25-12-173 § 912.5; NFPA 14 § 6.4.5.4).**
- Each separate sprinkler or standpipe system requires its own FDC (NFPA 13D excluded; stand-alone local <20-head systems excluded per FPCM 4.7.0). Street side, oriented to fire apparatus access, fully visible. Prohibited: under building overhangs, inside parking garages (even sprinklered), behind walls/fences, in 100-yr floodplain, in covered courtyards.
- **FDC-to-hydrant travel distance:** **100 ft** for standpipe systems (NFPA 14 § 6.4.5.4); **300 ft** for sprinklered buildings without Class I standpipe (IFC § 507.5.1.1). Working space: 36 in W × 36 in D × 78 in H; mounting 18–48 in above grade.
- High-rise: minimum **two remotely located FDCs** on separate building walls as far apart as possible (NFPA 14 § 7.12.2). For multi-zone standpipe systems, at least two FDCs per zone. FDC pressure demand ceiling: **150 psi** non-high-rise / **350 psi** high-rise (FPCM 4.8.0).
- Austin-amended FDC sign: white reflective letters on red, "FDC" ≥6 in tall, other words ≥2 in, approved text strings only ("FDC", "AUTOMATIC SPRINKLERS", "STANDPIPES", "TEST CONNECTION", combinations) — "FIRE DEPARTMENT CONNECTION" is **not** an approved string. Manual standpipes must indicate "MANUAL" + "WET"/"DRY"; PRV-equipped systems indicate floor range served.

**Fire area and high-rise classification.**
- Fire-flow calculation area = total gross floor area of all stories, mezzanines, basements, mechanical, and parking levels under exterior walls and horizontal roof projections (LDC § 25-12-173 B104.1). Exceptions: Type IA/IB → three largest successive floors (construction-type-based, **not** high-rise-based); open parking garage of IA/IB per IBC § 406.5 → single largest floor; R-3/R-4/townhouse/1–2-family separated <10 ft → combined.
- Fire walls per IBC § 706 create separate fire areas **only with zero openings**. Any fire door, damper, or utility penetration disqualifies the separation.
- Podium exclusion of garage from upper fire area (IBC § 510.2) requires **both** a 3-hr fire-rated horizontal assembly with no openings **and** NFPA 13 (not 13R) in the garage.
- High-rise threshold: any occupied floor >75 ft above the lowest level of fire department vehicle access (lowest finished grade of any adjacent fire lane / street; sloped sites use the downhill side). Standpipe trigger: highest floor >30 ft above same datum (IFC § 905.3.1). NFPA 13R disallowed for buildings ≥4 stories or with highest occupied floor ≥30 ft above lowest FD access (IFC § 903.3.1.2).
- Aerial-apparatus clearance review begins at ~73 ft per AFD operational practice — design overhead, planter, and side-yard clearances accordingly.

**WUI (LDC § 25-12-183).** Proximity Zones A (≤50 ft from ≥40 ac wildland), B (>50 ≤150 ft), C (>150 ft ≤0.5 mi from ≥40 ac, or within 1.5 mi of ≥750 ac). Most restrictive zone applies to the entire structure when it spans multiple zones. ETJ exempt.

**Underground fire main + utility interface (UCM 2.9.2.B.6; NFPA 13/24).**
- Service from public main to property line: **ductile iron** (DI); gate valve at the tap to the public main; backflow preventer inside property line, accessible for City inspection; **flow detection device** on every unmetered fire line, positioned so ≤100 gallons sit between the device and the public main.
- **NFPA 13 minimum fire service main: 6 in** (NFPA 13 § 24.1.3.1); smaller permitted only with PE-sealed hydraulic calc from a TX-licensed RME sprinkler designer. **Underground may extend ≤10 ft under building** (NFPA 13 § 10.4.3.1; NFPA 24 § 10.6.1); >10 ft triggers trench requirements (rigid walls, noncombustible base, accessible from within, drain, restrained joints, shutoff valve, freeze protection).
- Sectional control valves required when the private fire main serves **≥7 fire-protection connections** (NFPA 24 § 6.6.1). Each private hydrant gets a gate valve at the tee, restrained to the main with bolt-through connection (UCM 2.9.2.C.1). Fully restrained joints throughout (UCM 2.9.2.D).
- **NFPA 13 exterior shutoff** (NFPA 13 § 8.16.1) — one of: underground PIV ≥40 ft from building; wall-mounted PIV; exterior door direct to riser room within 15 ft walking distance (not under overhang); BFP vault (no hydrants downstream of BFP, no PIV upstream of BFP, no other valves in vault). PIVs not required for NFPA 13R/13D.
- High-rise fire pumps require **two water main connections** with independent supply piping each sized for full pump demand (UCM 2.9.2.A.3.e). Same-main exception only with valving between tap points. Buildings >420 ft: connections must be in **different streets** (IFC § 914.3.1.2). Parallel supply mains require ≥10 ft separation.

**Knox Box / Knox Switch (FPCM 4.4.0; FPCM Appendix E § 3.2.16; IFC § 506.1).**

# Parkland Dedication Feasibility — Austin

## Domain

Parkland dedication obligations, fee-in-lieu calculation, in-kind land dedication, public access easements, and on-site trail/recreation amenities required by City of Austin Parks and Recreation Department (PARD). Includes related instruments: Parkland Dedication Determination (formerly the PED letter), Parkland Improvement Agreements, fiscal surety, and Chapter 26 process when work touches existing City parkland.

Excludes: detailed trail design (covered by `ta` discipline for off-street network connectivity; on-site trail geometric design pulled from PARD/TCM is referenced here only as it bears on amenity cost and feasibility), and landscape/tree protection (covered by `el` discipline).

## Authoritative sources

- **Current ordinance:** Austin LDC Chapter 25-1, Article 14, §§ 25-1-601 through 25-1-612 (effective January 1, 2024 per Ord. 20231130-087, which fully repealed and renumbered the prior Article 14)
- **Operating procedures:** PDOP Rule R161-16.15 (uses pre-2024 LDC cross-references; cite by PDOP section, not embedded LDC numbers)
- **Determination:** LDC § 25-1-610 (Parkland Dedication Determination, replacing the informal "PED letter")
- **Construction on City parkland:** Texas Parks and Wildlife Code, Chapter 26, operationalized by ECM § 5.4.1
- **Fee schedule:** PARD annual fee schedule, updated October 1 each year. State formula set by Texas HB 1526 (2023); the City has no discretion over formula structure.
- **Urban trail design (if amenities include trail):** TCM § 5.3 and Standard Detail 1302S-1
- **District overlays:** ERC Regulating Plan § 4.10.3; NBG 3.5.8.D; LDC Subchapter E § 2.7 (private common open space) and § 2.3.1 (Table B connectivity)

## Regulatory pathway

Parkland dedication in Austin attaches at **site plan** (for multifamily and hotel/motel) and at **subdivision** (for single-family residential). Commercial, retail, and industrial uses are **not** subject to parkland dedication — the prior commercial requirement (Ord. 20220915-053) was repealed January 1, 2024. Civic uses (43 classifications in LDC § 25-2-6(B)) are also outside the scope of § 25-1-601(C).

Sequence:
1. **Pre-application:** Request a **Parkland Dedication Determination** from the PARD Director under LDC § 25-1-610. The Director specifies the satisfaction method (land, fee, easement, or combination), required acreage, preferred dedication location, off-site proximity limit, and any trail/connectivity conditions. Validity: lesser of 2 years (LDC § 25-1-610(D)) or 1 year (PDOP 14.3.5(B)) — assume 1 year. The Determination becomes stale if unit count changes by more than 10%.
2. **At site plan submittal:** Coversheet note must reference the Determination, current LDC Article 14, satisfaction method, unit counts, exempt units, and CO-timing for any unpaid multifamily fee.
3. **Before site plan release** (multifamily) **or final plat approval** (single-family): legal instruments executed — fee simple deed and ORS-coordinated transfer package; or recorded park easement; or recorded private parkland access easement under LDC § 25-1-605(E).
4. **Before CO** (multifamily): fee paid per LDC § 25-1-609(B).
5. **If construction touches existing City parkland:** Chapter 26 process (Parks Board hearing → City Council easement) plus PIA/PIMA — months-long timeline, not a paperwork item.

Decision body: PARD Director administers; Land Use Commission for Subchapter E waivers; City Council for Chapter 26 easements.

## Constraints to evaluate

### Applicability and exemptions

- **Use types subject:** residential dwelling units and hotel/motel rooms only. Verify all units are non-exempt before relying on a fee figure (LDC § 25-1-601(C)).
- **Exempt unit categories** (LDC § 25-1-601(D)): SMART Housing-certified units (D)(3); units income-restricted under any municipal/county/state/federal affordable housing program (D)(4) — broader than SMART, includes LIHTC, HUD Section 8, etc.; prior dedication credits (D)(1); Travis County ETJ (D)(2). The (D)(3) and (D)(4) exemptions are independent — a project may stack them across different units.
- **Site in ETJ:** parkland dedication does **not** apply at site plan stage (LDC § 25-1-601(D)(2)). Confirm jurisdictional status; sites that straddle city limits must address each portion separately.

### Calculation — multifamily

- Formula: `[(# MF units × 0.005) + (# hotel/motel rooms × 0.004)] × Avg Land Value × (1/Density Factor)` where Density Factor = 1 Suburban, 4 Urban, 40 CBD (LDC § 25-1-608).
- **Geographic Area designation is not self-selectable.** The Suburban/Urban/CBD boundary ordinance is not in Bureau. Confirm via the Determination letter or explicit PARD comment. Do **not** infer from neighborhood name or zoning.
- Land dedication cap: 10% of gross site area (LDC § 25-1-603(D)).
- Payment timing: **before CO**, not site plan release (LDC § 25-1-609(B)).
- Reference rates (per multifamily unit, FY 2025): CBD $2,427.65; Urban $4,676.52; Suburban $2,544.94. Rates update October 1 — verify current schedule before relying on these for pro forma.

### Calculation — single-family

- Density-based residents-per-unit multipliers (LDC § 25-1-602(C)): Low Density ≤6 DU/acre = 2.8; Medium 6–12 DU/acre = 2.2; High >12 DU/acre = 1.7.
- Urban Core single-family cap: **15% of gross site area** (LDC § 25-1-602(E)). This is a ceiling, not a minimum; formula amounts above 15% are converted to fee-in-lieu for the remainder.
- Two distinct single-family fees apply: fee-in-lieu (§ 25-1-606) and the parkland development fee (§ 25-1-607). Both due before plat/site plan approval.

### Land dedication — physical eligibility (PDOP § 14.3.7)

- **Minimum parcel size:** ¼ acre per dedicated parcel (§ 14.3.7(A)(7)(a)).
- **Visibility:** interior *should* be visible from public ROW — ≥200 ft frontage per 2 acres for parks ≥2 acres; ≥half the widest dimension for parks <2 acres (§ 14.3.7(A)(1); "should," not "shall").
- **Grade and active-play:** ≥50% *should* be ≤10% grade, well-drained, suitable for active play (§ 14.3.7(A)(2); "should"). Exception for trail connections or environmental/cultural resource preservation.
- **Utility connections (mandatory):** potable water on all park sites; sewer on sites ≥2 acres (§ 14.3.7(A)(4)).
- **Encumbrances (mandatory):** no recorded easement that prevents amenity construction (§ 14.3.7(A)(3)). AE electrical easements and utility easements within the parkland boundary are common disqualifiers. Transmission easement land cannot be labeled or dedicated as parkland (UCM § 1.14.7).
- **Creek/water-body adjacency:** dedication must be by **fee simple deed**, not park easement (PARD reviewer convention — uniformly enforced).
- **Off-site dedication proximity:** ¼ mile within the Parkland Dedication Urban Core; ½ mile outside (PDOP § 14.3.7(B)). No 1½-mile alternative exists in current code despite older references.

### Partial credit framework (PDOP § 14.3.8)

The credit table must break out by encumbrance category. Common rates:

| Land condition | Credit |
|---|---|
| Unencumbered upland | up to 100% |
| 25-year floodplain | **0%** (must still be dedicated; no exception) |
| 100-year floodplain (outside 25-yr) | 50% — only if adjacent 25-yr floodplain is also included |
| CEF buffer / CWQZ where amenities **allowed** | 50% |
| CEF buffer / CWQZ where amenities **not allowed** | 0% |
| Water quality / detention pond with PARD-approved amenities | 50% |
| Fire lane functioning as a trail connecting to a larger system | 50% |

No 60% credit for trail or park easements exists in current PDOP — a credit table showing this is incorrect.

### Private parkland credit (LDC § 25-1-605)

Bridges to fire (FWP) on fire-flow adequacy and to SDUF on rainwater/condensate reuse intersecting with stormwater.

- Water/wastewater/reclaimed service area: Austin Water utility coverage = the AW "impact fee boundary" (UCM 2.2.1). Confirm against AW's GIS service-area layer; do not infer from full-purpose corporate limits alone.

- OSSF (septic) for parcels with no reachable public main: Austin City Code Chapter 15-5 (abandonment + within-corporate-limits OSSF); Travis County / Hays County / Williamson County permitting under TCEQ Chapter 285 in the ETJ.
- Industrial Waste Control Program (Chapter 15-10) — applies when AW is wastewater provider and discharge is non-domestic.
- Water Benchmarking Application (WBA/WBC): LDC § 25-9-413 (site plan submittal requirement).

## Regulatory pathway

| Action | Path / authority | Typical timing |
|---|---|---|
| Confirm service area + provider (AW vs MUD/WCID/CCN-holder) | AW GIS + PUC CCN map; LDC § 25-9-33(C)(2) | Day 0 (diligence) |
| Service availability letter (water + WW) | AW; must be dated within 6 months of review | 4-8 weeks |

| WW SER multi-department review (AFD + Industrial Waste) | LDC § 25-9-33(C)(3), § 25-9-34(B) | Folded into SER timeline |
| Water Benchmarking Application (WBA/WBC) | LDC § 25-9-413(A); at site plan submittal | Concurrent with site plan |
| Large-development (GFA ≥ 250,000 SF) director consultation | LDC § 25-9-413(B) | Before site plan filing |
| AULCC (utility coordination) review for ROW work | UCM 3.2.0 | Plan set delivered 2 weeks before meeting |
| Reclaimed connection eligibility check (250 / 500 ft) | LDC § 25-9-412 | At concept; verify with AW Reclaimed Group |

| OSSF permit (ETJ, where no public main within 100 ft) | TCEQ Chapter 285 via county | Soil eval + 30-90 days |
| Easement recordation (if AW infrastructure outside ROW) | UCM 2.9.1.A.1-A.4; AWPE pre-recordation review | Before AW plan approval |

### Service area + provider

- **Is the parcel inside Austin Water's retail service area?** AW serves within its impact-fee boundary (UCM 2.2.1). Full-purpose annexation does not automatically mean AW is the retail provider. Common Austin-area alternatives:
  - **Northtown MUD** (north Austin / Pflugerville fringe) — UCM 2.5.1.B requires its prior written approval before AW will sign anything.
  - **Southwest Water / Mid-Tex** — west / southwest ETJ.
  - **City of Manor** — eastern fringe.
  - **WCIDs** — scattered (e.g., WCID 17 in westlake).
- If a non-AW provider holds the CCN, expect a CCN release or transfer through PUC before AW can serve (LDC § 25-9-33(C)(2)). This adds 6-18 months and is not always achievable.
- If site is **inside the ETJ**, design must still meet COA standards but Industrial Waste plans go directly to the IW office, not through DSD (UCM 2.5.1.F).

### Capacity — water

- AW does **not** publish reservation; an approved SER is "acknowledgment of intent to serve" only (UCM 2.2.3(E)).
- **Pressure Concern Area** — administrative AW designation where existing infrastructure cannot maintain 20 psi residual at peak day + fire flow (UCM 2.9.2.A.3.d) or stays under 10 fps emergency velocity (UCM 2.9.2.A.3.c). Triggers a Water SER under LDC § 25-9-33(A)(3). Not mappable from public data — confirm via AW correspondence.
- **Pressure zone** must be designated on the AW General Info Sheet; affects pump sizing on tall buildings.
- Minimum public water main = 8 inches (UCM 2.9.2.A.4.a). Mains ≥24 inches are **transmission mains** (LDC § 25-9-32(15)) — no meter or fire-line tap permitted without a Director exception, even with an approved SER.
- Fire flow per FPCM Table 507-1: 1,000 gpm floor for SF < 3,600 SF; 2,500-3,500 gpm typical for multifamily / commercial. The 1,000 gpm number is a floor, not a default.

### Capacity — wastewater

- **Wastewater Capacity Concern Area** — administrative AW designation; not codified or mapped publicly. Triggers a WW SER under LDC § 25-9-33(A)(3). Confirm via AW correspondence; do not assume capacity from a 5-year-old AW master-plan study.

- Gravity service is required where feasible (UCM 2.9.4.J); lift stations are disfavored. If the city main is a **force main**, a grinder station at the property line is required and distance from property line to a gravity main must be ≤200 ft (UCM 2.9.4.J.18).

### SER triggers (LDC § 25-9-33(A))

An SER is required when any of:
1. Nearest accessible main is **>100 ft** from the property boundary.
2. Proposed connection is to a transmission main (≥24") or interceptor (≥18").
3. Existing main is unsuitable / insufficient (pressure concern, capacity concern, lot-line-crossing private piping, alley main connections, water meters on private lines, force-main extensions, public WW extension >100 ft, etc.).
4. Service is from a decentralized WW system the Director recommends the City operate.

Additional design-time triggers that may not strictly trigger an SER but constrain layout:
- Wastewater direct service tap prohibited to any main >15" (UCM 2.9.4.G.3) — applies even where the LDC § 25-9-32(14) interceptor threshold (≥18") isn't met.
- Water meters must be placed in public ROW or in an easement immediately adjacent to ROW; meters inside fences or on private lines are non-compliant (UCM 2.9.2.E.3).

**SER carries an expiration**: 180 days from approval (post-April 2013, LDC § 25-9-39(C)) — extended by a pending or approved development application, indefinite for recorded-plat portions.     24→**Severity:** significant | moderate | note | data-gap | opportunity
    25→**Citation:** <code section, GIS layer, program reference>
    26→**Finding:** 2-4 sentences. Factual. State what the constraint or opportunity is and what evidence supports it.

    50→|---|---|
    51→| `significant` | Project-altering: prohibition, >$100k cost delta, >6mo delay, loss of units |
    52→| `moderate` | Material but workable: design constraint, <$50k delta, <3mo delay |

```markdown
**Implication for the developer:** 1-2 sentences. What changes for them? Cost, timeline, design, risk.
**Recommended next step:** 1 sentence. Concrete action.

### <Finding 2 — short title>
...

## Plan-specific findings
Only if a concept plan was provided. Same shape as Findings, but tied to specific plan features:

### <Plan-specific finding 1>
**Severity:** ...
**Drawing reference:** <page, callout, dimension>
**Finding:** How does the proposed plan respond to the constraint?
**Compliance status:** complies | does not comply | unclear
**Implication for the developer:** ...

## Open questions for the engineer
Bullets. Only items that need engineer judgment, not items we should have answered ourselves.
```

## Severity rules

| Level | Threshold |
|---|---|
| `significant` | Project-altering: prohibition, >$100k cost delta, >6mo delay, loss of units |
| `moderate` | Material but workable: design constraint, <$50k delta, <3mo delay |
| `note` | Worth knowing, not feasibility-altering |
| `data-gap` | Couldn't determine; specific recommended source |
| `opportunity` | Affirmative upside (density bonus, expedited path, fee reduction) |

Use the discipline's feasibility-guide severity heuristics — they may further specialize these thresholds.

## Citations are mandatory

Every finding cites:
- A code section (`Austin LDC § 25-8-281`), AND/OR
- A GIS layer or specific data source (`Travis County GIS — Watershed Protection layer`), AND/OR
- A program reference (`HOME Initiative Phase 1, City Council Resolution 20231214-XYZ`)

If you can't cite, you're guessing — go find the source or remove the claim.

## What not to do

- Don't speculate ("might be", "could potentially") — say what the source shows or mark `data-gap`
- Don't issue a "consult a specialist" recommendation without first scoping the question (what specifically would the specialist confirm?)
- Don't duplicate findings that cross disciplines — surface them once in the discipline they're primary to, and cross-reference from other disciplines
- Don't apply rules from one jurisdiction to another (Austin's heritage tree CRZ rules don't apply in Jarrell unless Jarrell has adopted them)

## Cross-references

If your finding overlaps with another discipline:
- Heritage tree → primary in `eptp`, cross-ref from `el`, `fwp`, `sde`
- Floodplain → primary in `fwp`, cross-ref from `el`, `sde`
- Stormwater → primary in `sde`, cross-ref from `el`, `wwp`
- Parking → primary in `zlu`, cross-ref from `sduf`, `ta`

Note cross-references as `(see also: <discipline> — <finding>)` in the finding body, not as separate findings.

# Restrictive Covenants & Recorded Instruments Research

**Property:** 9101 Cameron Rd, Austin, TX 78753
**Parcel ID:** 928312 (TCAD)
**Legal description:** UNIT 1 CAMERON FERGUSON CONDOMINIUMS DOC NO. 2018119069 O.P.R.T.C.T.

## Summary

This research covers the recorded instruments visible on the concept plan, the condominium declaration governing the subject unit, and the original subdivision (Trigg Addition). No county clerk PDFs were downloaded for this run (surveyor CLI not invoked); instrument analysis is based on the concept plan callouts, TCAD records, and web research.

## Findings

### Condominium Declaration — Cameron Ferguson Condominiums (Doc. No. 2018119069)
**Citation:** Travis County Official Public Records, Doc. No. 2018119069, O.P.R.T.C.T.
**What it means for development:** The subject parcel is Unit 1 of the Cameron Ferguson Condominiums. This condominium regime was established in 2018 and divides a larger parent tract into separately owned units. The declaration defines the unit boundaries, common elements, exclusive-use common elements, maintenance obligations, and potentially use restrictions or architectural controls. Key development implications:
- The condominium declaration may restrict the types of commercial uses permitted within Unit 1, or impose design/signage standards beyond what CS zoning requires.
- Common elements (driveways, utilities, stormwater infrastructure) may be shared with adjacent units (Unit 4 to the south per the concept plan).
- Any site modifications affecting common elements may require approval from the condominium association or other unit owners.
- The condominium plat (Resubdivision of Cameron Ferguson Park, Doc. No. 201800004) is the controlling plat; modifications may require a plat amendment.
**Confidence:** Inferred from concept plan callouts and TCAD records. The actual declaration text was not reviewed — this is a data gap.

### Resubdivision of Cameron Ferguson Park (Doc. No. 201800004)
**Citation:** Travis County Official Public Records, Doc. No. 201800004, O.P.R.T.C.T.
**What it means for development:** This is the controlling plat/resubdivision document that created the current lot configuration. The concept plan shows this instrument associated with Block A and the 25' R.O.W. Reserve. The resubdivision likely established:
- Lot lines, building setback lines, and easement locations
- The 25' R.O.W. reserve along Cameron Rd (for future ROW dedication)
- Drainage and utility easement locations
- Plat notes with conditions of approval
**Confidence:** Inferred from concept plan. Actual plat notes not reviewed — data gap.

### Trigg Addition (Volume 68, Page 79, P.R.T.C.T.)
**Citation:** Travis County Plat Records, Volume 68, Page 79
**What it means for development:** Trigg Addition is the original subdivision plat covering this area. Recorded in the plat records (P.R.T.C.T. = Plat Records, Travis County, Texas), this is a very old plat (Volume 68 suggests mid-20th century). Key questions:
- Old subdivisions in Austin sometimes include deed restrictions (setbacks, use limitations, minimum lot size) that run with the land. If Trigg Addition deed restrictions exist and have not expired, they could impose setback or use constraints beyond current zoning.
- The age of the plat suggests that any original deed restrictions may have expired under their own terms (common 25-year or 30-year expiration clauses) or been superseded by the 2018 resubdivision.
- The concept plan shows this instrument associated with the adjacent property to the east (D & M Precision / Precision Engine Service, 44,150 SF / 1.014 acres), suggesting the subject parcel may have been replatted out of Trigg Addition.
**Confidence:** Unconfirmed. Trigg Addition deed restrictions should be pulled and reviewed. The resubdivision in 2018 likely addressed or superseded original plat restrictions, but this needs verification.

### Electric Easement (Doc. No. 2013157214)
**Citation:** Travis County Official Public Records, Doc. No. 2013157214, O.P.R.T.C.T.
**What it means for development:** An electric utility easement crossing the property. The concept plan shows this easement on the western portion of the site. Development within this easement is restricted — no permanent structures, foundations, or deep-rooted landscaping within Austin Energy easements. The easement location may constrain building placement and landscaping in the western portion of the site.
**Confidence:** Verified from concept plan. Easement width and exact centerline not legible from available crops.

### Drainage Easement (Doc. No. 2014138374)
**Citation:** Travis County Official Public Records, Doc. No. 2014138374, O.P.R.T.C.T.
**What it means for development:** A drainage easement crossing the southern portion of the property. This easement is likely associated with the existing 24" storm line and grate inlets shown on the concept plan. Development within drainage easements is prohibited without Director approval and a license/encroachment agreement. The preliminary pond shown on the concept plan appears to be located outside this easement.
**Confidence:** Verified from concept plan. Exact width not measured.

### 10' Public Utility Easement (Doc. No. 200800021)
**Citation:** Travis County Official Public Records, Doc. No. 200800021, O.P.R.T.C.T.
**What it means for development:** A 10-foot-wide public utility easement. The concept plan shows this PUE on the southern/southeastern boundary area. Standard PUE restrictions apply: no permanent structures within the easement; utilities may be routed through it. The building footprint must be outside this easement.
**Confidence:** Verified from concept plan.

### 7.5' Public Utility Easement (Doc. No. 200800021)
**Citation:** Travis County Official Public Records, Doc. No. 200800021, O.P.R.T.C.T.
**What it means for development:** A 7.5-foot-wide PUE, also from the same instrument as the 10' PUE. Shown on the eastern property boundary area. Same restrictions as the 10' PUE.
**Confidence:** Verified from concept plan.

### 25' Right-of-Way Reserve (Doc. No. 201800004)
**Citation:** Travis County Official Public Records, Doc. No. 201800004, O.P.R.T.C.T.
**What it means for development:** A 25-foot R.O.W. reserve along Cameron Road, established by the 2018 resubdivision. This reserve is designated for future ROW dedication to the City of Austin as part of Cameron Rd improvements per the Austin Strategic Mobility Plan. Key implications:
- The reserve area cannot be counted toward buildable area or setback calculations
- ROW dedication will be required at site plan — the "Potential ROW Dedication" area shown on the concept plan aligns with this reserve
- The preliminary pond is positioned partially within or adjacent to this reserve area, which may create a conflict
**Confidence:** Verified from concept plan.

### 15' Wastewater Easement (Vol. 11285, Pg. 2104)
**Citation:** Travis County Records, Volume 11285, Page 2104
**What it means for development:** A 15-foot-wide wastewater easement. The concept plan shows two 15' W.W.E. callouts — one associated with this deed record and another in the right-of-way area. These easements protect the existing 8" and 10" wastewater lines shown on the plan. No permanent structures may be placed within these easements, and wastewater main access must be maintained.
**Confidence:** Verified from concept plan.

### Varying Water Easement
**Citation:** Document reference partially visible on concept plan, O.P.R.T.C.T.
**What it means for development:** A water easement with varying width. This likely protects the existing 36" and/or 14" water lines along or near Cameron Road. A 36" water line is a transmission main — Austin Water typically requires wider easements for transmission mains (15' minimum or 2× depth per UCM 2.9.1.A.1). The exact width and location should be confirmed from the recorded instrument.

# Phase 2 Environmental Research

**Property:** 9101 Cameron Rd, Austin, TX 78753
**Parcel ID:** 928312 (TCAD)
**Lot Area:** 44,150 SF (1.01 AC)
**Zoning:** CS (General Commercial Services)
**Proposed Use:** AutoZone retail store, 7,375 SF single-story
**Research Date:** 2026-06-04

---

## 1. Watershed Classification

**Finding:** The property at 9101 Cameron Rd is located within the **Little Walnut Creek watershed**, which is classified as an **Urban Watershed** under the City of Austin's Watershed Protection Ordinance (WPO). Little Walnut Creek is a tributary of Walnut Creek, which drains approximately 43 square miles of northern Austin before discharging to the Colorado River. The Urban Watershed classification was established by the Urban Watersheds Ordinance (UWO) adopted in 1991 and later incorporated into the Comprehensive Watersheds Ordinance framework.

Urban Watersheds in Austin are governed by LDC Chapter 25-8, Subchapter A, Article 8 (Urban Watershed Requirements). The urban designation reflects the heavily developed character of the surrounding area and applies the least restrictive tier of watershed regulations among Austin's four categories (Urban, Suburban, Water Supply Suburban, Water Supply Rural).

**Citation:** Austin LDC Ch. 25-8, Subchapter A, Art. 8 (Urban Watershed Requirements); City of Austin Watershed Regulation Areas GIS layer (data.austintexas.gov, dataset 2xkn-3rmn); City of Austin Watershed Boundaries dataset (yfaf-uvsu).

**Development Impact:** As an Urban Watershed site, the property is subject to water quality controls for new impervious cover but benefits from the most permissive impervious cover regime. The key regulatory burden is the requirement for structural water quality treatment rather than impervious cover caps.

**Confidence:** Verified -- Little Walnut Creek is consistently identified as an Urban Watershed in City of Austin regulatory materials and GIS datasets.

---

## 2. Critical Environmental Features (CEFs)

**Finding:** The concept plan for 9101 Cameron Rd shows **CEF setback (CEF STBK) lines** on the eastern and northeastern portions of the site. Under Austin's Environmental Criteria Manual (ECM) Section 1.10.0 and LDC Section 25-8-281, Critical Environmental Features include springs, seeps, bluffs, canyon rimrock, caves, sinkholes, and wetlands. The presence of CEF setback lines on the concept plan indicates that at least one mapped or field-identified CEF exists on or adjacent to the parcel.

Given the site's topography (gentle slope NE to SW, elevation 626-636 ft) and the presence of mapped CWQZ boundaries, the CEFs on or near this site are most likely **springs or seeps** associated with the drainage features crossing the property, rather than bluffs or canyon rimrock (which require 40+ ft vertical relief at steep grades, not present here).

**Standard CEF buffer requirements (ECM 1.10.4):**
- Default buffer: **150 feet** from the edge of the CEF
- Springs/seeps: may be administratively reduced to a minimum of **50 feet** with site-specific hydrogeologic justification demonstrating preservation of flow quantity and quality
- Reductions below 50 feet require a **Land Use Commission variance** per LDC 25-8-41

**Citation:** Austin LDC Section 25-8-281 (Critical Environmental Features); ECM Section 1.10.0, 1.10.3, 1.10.4 (CEF Identification and Protection); City of Austin Biologic Resource Buffers (CEF Setbacks) GIS layer (data.austintexas.gov, dataset n7cy-835m).

**Development Impact:** The CEF setback areas shown on the eastern/northeastern portion of the site are **non-buildable** unless a variance or administrative reduction is obtained. The proposed building footprint appears to be positioned west of the CEF setback lines, which is appropriate. Any grading, paving, or utility installation within the CEF buffer is prohibited absent an approved exception. A field survey and Environmental Resource Inventory (ERI) will be required to confirm CEF locations and negotiate final buffer dimensions with the Watershed Protection Department.

**Confidence:** Verified (CEF setbacks shown on concept plan) / Inferred (specific CEF type likely spring or seep based on terrain).

**Finding:** The concept plan confirms that **CWQZ boundaries cross the site in multiple locations**. # Transportation Research -- Phase 2

**Property:** 9101 Cameron Rd, Austin, TX 78753
**Parcel ID:** 928312 (TCAD)
**Zoning:** CS (General Commercial Services)
**Proposed Use:** AutoZone retail store, 7,375 SF
**Jurisdiction:** City of Austin

---

## 1. ASMP Street Classification -- Cameron Road

**Finding:** Cameron Road is classified as **ASMP Street Level 4** in the Austin Strategic Mobility Plan Street Network. Level 4 streets are designated for **"Corridor Mobility"** -- the second-highest tier in Austin's five-level street hierarchy. The ASMP GIS layer confirms the classification applies to segments in the vicinity of 9101 Cameron Rd. The street currently has **6 travel lanes** (existing configuration), and the future cross-section also specifies 6 travel lanes. The project type is listed as "Corridor Mobility Improvements" involving "mobility, safety, and connectivity improvements to accommodate multiple modes of transportation, including driving, walking, biking, and taking transit."

**Target Cross-Section:** The ASMP data indicates a future cross-section maintaining 6 travel lanes with addition of protected bicycle facilities and enhanced pedestrian infrastructure. The Cameron Road / Dessau Road Safety Project (funded through the 2020 Mobility Bond and a 2022 Safe Streets and Roads for All federal grant) proposes reconfiguring from three lanes in each direction to two lanes in each direction between US 290 and Parmer Lane, with strategic turn lanes retained at major intersections. Note: this reconfiguration primarily applies to the segment north of US 183; the segment near 9101 Cameron Rd (south of US 183) may retain its existing 6-lane configuration.

**Required ROW Width:** The ASMP GIS data shows a **required ROW of 154 feet** for Cameron Road segments in this area. Current mean ROW ranges from approximately **98.6 to 116 feet** depending on the segment.

**Citation:** City of Austin, ASMP Street Network GIS Layer (ID: 7), queried via ArcGIS REST API; Cameron Road / Dessau Road Safety Project StoryMap (storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/b8bec12a854d45c9b8b4721ff73f5915).

**Development Implication:** The gap between existing ROW (approximately 99--116 ft) and the 154 ft target ROW means ROW dedication will almost certainly be required at time of development. This is consistent with the concept plan notation of "Potential ROW Dedication" and "25' R.O.W. Reserve (Doc. No. 201800004)." The Level 4 classification triggers more stringent access management requirements and may limit the number and type of driveways.

**Confidence:** HIGH -- Classification confirmed via direct GIS query of the ASMP layer; ROW data from same source.

---

## 2. ROW Dedication

**Finding:** ROW dedication will be required. The ASMP data confirms:
- **Existing mean ROW:** Approximately 99--116 feet (varies by segment)
- **Target ROW:** 154 feet
- **Dedication needed:** Approximately 19--27.5 feet per side (assuming symmetric dedication from current conditions), though the actual amount will depend on the specific segment geometry and which side of the roadway is deficient.

The concept plan already depicts a "Potential ROW Dedication" area along the Cameron Road frontage and references a "25' R.O.W. Reserve (Doc. No. 201800004)," which is consistent with the gap between existing and target ROW. The ASMP coordination notes state that "ROW dedication may be necessary through the land development process for new development and commercial redevelopment."

Additionally, the Cameron Road / Dessau Road Safety Project is actively under construction (groundbreaking October 2025), and the City may use the site plan review process to secure additional ROW from this parcel to support corridor improvements.

**Citation:** ASMP Street Network GIS Layer; Cameron/Dessau Safety Project FAQ (austintexas.gov/sites/default/files/files/TPW/Bond/Cameron-Dessau_FAQs_ENG_10-2024.pdf); concept plan reference to Doc. No. 201800004.

**Development Implication:** The applicant should budget for loss of developable area along the Cameron Road frontage. A 25-foot dedication (as shown on the concept plan) would reduce the available site depth. The dedication will need to be conveyed at no cost to the City as a condition of site plan approval. The building footprint, parking layout, and stormwater management areas must be designed to accommodate the post-dedication parcel geometry.

**Confidence:** HIGH -- Concept plan already shows the dedication; ASMP data confirms the ROW gap.

---

## 3. Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA)

**Finding:** A 7,375 SF AutoZone retail store is **unlikely to trigger a full TIA** under current City of Austin thresholds.

**Threshold:** The City of Austin requires a TIA when a proposed development generates more than **2,000 vehicle trips per day**. A full TIA is required for projects generating more than **5,000 vehicle trips per day**; projects between 2,000 and 5,000 trips/day may be subject to a smaller traffic assessment focused on sustainable modes and Transportation Demand Management (TDM).

1→# Site Plan & Form Findings -- 9101 Cameron Rd
     2→
     3→**Property:** 9101 Cameron Rd, Austin, TX 78753 | CS zoning | 1.01 AC / 44,150 SF
     4→**Proposed:** AutoZone retail store (Retail Sale of Auto Parts), 7,375 SF Prototype 74, single-story, 12 parking spaces, preliminary pond
     5→**Discipline:** Site Plan & Form (SDUF)
     6→**Date:** 2026-06-04
     7→
     8→---
     9→
    10→## Summary
    11→
    12→- **Subchapter E (Design Standards and Mixed Use) applies.** The project is a nonresidential commercial development requiring a site plan on a principal street (Cameron Rd, ASMP Level 4). It is not exempt from Subchapter E. Articles 2 and 3 govern site development standards and building design standards, respectively.
    13→- **The concept plan's parking-in-front-of-building layout is a likely Subchapter E conflict.** The concept plan shows the building set back from Cameron Rd with surface parking and the preliminary pond between the building and the street. Subchapter E Section 2.2 restricts or prohibits surface parking between a building and the principal street, with the strictness depending on whether Cameron Rd is classified as an Urban Roadway or Suburban Roadway. This is the most significant site plan risk identified.
    14→- **Entrance orientation toward Cameron Rd is required.** Section 2.4 requires the primary customer entrance to face the principal street and be architecturally prominent and visible from the abutting street. The AutoZone Prototype 74 layout must be evaluated for compliance.
    15→- **Building design standards (Article 3) require glazing, articulation, and blank-wall treatment on the Cameron Rd facade.** The principal-street-facing elevation must meet transparency requirements (40% glazing on the front facade, 25% on publicly visible sides, VT of 0.6 or higher) and must incorporate design elements at the primary entrance.
    16→- **Site Plan Lite does not apply.** Site Plan Lite (Phase 1 and Phase 2) targets residential projects (single-family through 16-unit residential). A 7,375 SF single-tenant commercial retail building requires a standard administrative site plan, not Site Plan Lite.
    17→- **The procedural path is administrative site plan review by DSD staff.** No commission or council hearing is triggered. Alternative Equivalent Compliance (AEC) is available if the prototype design cannot strictly meet Subchapter E standards.
    18→
    19→---
    20→
    21→## Procedural Path
    22→
    23→| Element | Determination | Citation |
    24→|---|---|---|
    25→| **Site plan required?** | Yes -- commercial development on 1.01 AC requiring new building, parking, drainage | LDC 25-5-1 |
    26→| **Site plan type** | Administrative (standard) site plan | LDC 25-5-1; 25-5-3 |
    27→| **Site Plan Lite eligible?** | No -- applies to residential projects (up to 16 units under Phase 2); this is single-tenant commercial retail | Ord. 20250306 (SPL Phase 2); LDC 25-5 |
    28→| **Small project exemption?** | No -- proposed IC of 16,666 SF exceeds the 5,000 SF IC threshold for small projects; construction area of 7,375 SF exceeds 10,000 SF threshold when site improvements are included | LDC 25-5-3 |
    29→| **Approval authority** | DSD Director (administrative, staff-level) | LDC 25-5-5 |
    30→| **Commission/Council hearing?** | No -- no conditional use, variance, or rezoning triggers identified | LDC 25-5; 25-1-501 |
    31→| **Notification required?** | Yes -- standard site plan notification to adjacent property owners | LDC 25-5-4 |
    32→| **Subchapter E applies?** | Yes -- nonresidential site plan on principal street (Cameron Rd) | LDC 25-2, Subchapter E, Art. 1 |
    33→
    34→---
    35→
    36→## Findings
    37→
    38→### SDUF-1: Subchapter E Applies -- Cameron Rd as Principal Street
    39→
    40→**Severity:** Informational (procedural)
    41→**Citation:** LDC 25-2, Subchapter E, Article 1 (Applicability); Article 5 (Definitions); ASMP Street Network Table
    42→**Finding:** Subchapter E applies to all nonresidential and mixed-use development requiring a site plan, with applicability determined by Table A based on the principal street classification and development type. Cameron Rd is classified as ASMP Level 4. Under Subchapter E Section 2.1, roadways are classified into three types -- Urban Roadway, Suburban Roadway, and Hill Country Roadway -- based on location, context, and Imagine Austin designation. Level 4 roads in the Cameron Rd corridor (north Austin, outside the urban core, not within an Imagine Austin activity center or core transit corridor) are most likely classified as Suburban Roadway. However, this classification must be confirmed with DSD during pre-application, as Cameron Rd's context may support Urban Roadway classification in certain segments, particularly if it falls within an Imagine Austin activity corridor.
    43→**Implication:** The Suburban vs. Urban Roadway classification directly affects the stringency of build-to zone, parking placement, and frontage requirements. If classified as Urban Roadway, the constraints on the current layout are more severe.
    44→**Next step:** Confirm Cameron Rd's Subchapter E roadway classification with DSD at pre-application. Request the Subchapter E applicability determination letter.
    45→
    46→---
    47→
    48→### SDUF-2: Parking Placement Between Building and Principal Street -- Likely Noncompliance (HIGH RISK)
    49→
    50→**Severity:** High
    51→**Citation:** LDC 25-2, Subchapter E, Section 2.2 (Building Placement)
    52→**Finding:** The concept plan shows the AutoZone building set back from Cameron Rd with surface parking and the preliminary stormwater pond positioned between the building and the Cameron Rd frontage. Subchapter E Section 2.2 restricts surface parking between the building and the principal street:
    53→
    54→- **If Urban Roadway:** Parking between the building and the property line adjacent to the principal street is prohibited, except on sites 400 feet deep or less where parking may be located between the street and the building only if certain frontage build-out conditions are met (e.g., 40% of net frontage consists of continuous building facade built up to the clear zone). Even under this exception, the current layout -- where the building is fully set back behind a parking lot -- is unlikely to qualify.
    55→- **If Suburban Roadway:** Standards are less restrictive but still require either (a) the building to be pulled up to the sidewalk/clear zone for a specified percentage of net frontage, or (b) if parking is placed in front, the site must satisfy alternative connectivity and design requirements. The Suburban Roadway classification provides the best path for the current layout but still imposes conditions.
    56→
    57→The concept plan's layout -- building behind parking with the pond between the building and Cameron Rd -- is a classic Subchapter E conflict for auto-parts retail prototypes. AutoZone's Prototype 74 typically places the storefront facing the parking lot with the building set back, which conflicts with Subchapter E's urban-form objectives.
    58→
    59→**Implication:** This is the single largest site plan risk. The building will likely need to be repositioned closer to Cameron Rd, with parking relocated to the side or rear. # Site Plan & Form Findings -- 9101 Cameron Rd

**Property:** 9101 Cameron Rd, Austin, TX 78753 | CS zoning | 1.01 AC / 44,150 SF
**Proposed:** AutoZone retail store (Retail Sale of Auto Parts), 7,375 SF Prototype 74, single-story, 12 parking spaces, preliminary pond
**Discipline:** Site Plan & Form (SDUF)
**Date:** 2026-06-04

---

## Summary

- **Subchapter E (Design Standards and Mixed Use) applies.** The project is a nonresidential commercial development requiring a site plan on a principal street (Cameron Rd, ASMP Level 4). It is not exempt from Subchapter E. Articles 2 and 3 govern site development standards and building design standards, respectively.
- **The concept plan's parking-in-front-of-building layout is a likely Subchapter E conflict.** The concept plan shows the building set back from Cameron Rd with surface parking and the preliminary pond between the building and the street. Subchapter E Section 2.2 restricts or prohibits surface parking between a building and the principal street, with the strictness depending on whether Cameron Rd is classified as an Urban Roadway or Suburban Roadway. This is the most significant site plan risk identified.
- **Entrance orientation toward Cameron Rd is required.** Section 2.4 requires the primary customer entrance to face the principal street and be architecturally prominent and visible from the abutting street. The AutoZone Prototype 74 layout must be evaluated for compliance.
- **Building design standards (Article 3) require glazing, articulation, and blank-wall treatment on the Cameron Rd facade.** The principal-street-facing elevation must meet transparency requirements (40% glazing on the front facade, 25% on publicly visible sides, VT of 0.6 or higher) and must incorporate design elements at the primary entrance.
- **Site Plan Lite does not apply.** Site Plan Lite (Phase 1 and Phase 2) targets residential projects (single-family through 16-unit residential). A 7,375 SF single-tenant commercial retail building requires a standard administrative site plan, not Site Plan Lite.
- **The procedural path is administrative site plan review by DSD staff.** No commission or council hearing is triggered. Alternative Equivalent Compliance (AEC) is available if the prototype design cannot strictly meet Subchapter E standards.

---

## Procedural Path

| Element | Determination | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| **Site plan required?** | Yes -- commercial development on 1.01 AC requiring new building, parking, drainage | LDC 25-5-1 |
| **Site plan type** | Administrative (standard) site plan | LDC 25-5-1; 25-5-3 |
| **Site Plan Lite eligible?** | No -- applies to residential projects (up to 16 units under Phase 2); this is single-tenant commercial retail | Ord. 20250306 (SPL Phase 2); LDC 25-5 |
| **Small project exemption?** | No -- proposed IC of 16,666 SF exceeds the 5,000 SF IC threshold for small projects; construction area of 7,375 SF exceeds 10,000 SF threshold when site improvements are included | LDC 25-5-3 |
| **Approval authority** | DSD Director (administrative, staff-level) | LDC 25-5-5 |
| **Commission/Council hearing?** | No -- no conditional use, variance, or rezoning triggers identified | LDC 25-5; 25-1-501 |
| **Notification required?** | Yes -- standard site plan notification to adjacent property owners | LDC 25-5-4 |
| **Subchapter E applies?** | Yes -- nonresidential site plan on principal street (Cameron Rd) | LDC 25-2, Subchapter E, Art. 1 |

---

## Findings

### SDUF-1: Subchapter E Applies -- Cameron Rd as Principal Street

**Severity:** Informational (procedural)
**Citation:** LDC 25-2, Subchapter E, Article 1 (Applicability); Article 5 (Definitions); ASMP Street Network Table
**Finding:** Subchapter E applies to all nonresidential and mixed-use development requiring a site plan, with applicability determined by Table A based on the principal street classification and development type. Cameron Rd is classified as ASMP Level 4. Under Subchapter E Section 2.1, roadways are classified into three types -- Urban Roadway, Suburban Roadway, and Hill Country Roadway -- based on location, context, and Imagine Austin designation. Level 4 roads in the Cameron Rd corridor (north Austin, outside the urban core, not within an Imagine Austin activity center or core transit corridor) are most likely classified as Suburban Roadway. However, this classification must be confirmed with DSD during pre-application, as Cameron Rd's context may support Urban Roadway classification in certain segments, particularly if it falls within an Imagine Austin activity corridor.
**Implication:** The Suburban vs. Urban Roadway classification directly affects the stringency of build-to zone, parking placement, and frontage requirements. If classified as Urban Roadway, the constraints on the current layout are more severe.
**Next step:** Confirm Cameron Rd's Subchapter E roadway classification with DSD at pre-application. Request the Subchapter E applicability determination letter.

---

### SDUF-2: Parking Placement Between Building and Principal Street -- Likely Noncompliance (HIGH RISK)

**Severity:** High
**Citation:** LDC 25-2, Subchapter E, Section 2.2 (Building Placement)
**Finding:** The concept plan shows the AutoZone building set back from Cameron Rd with surface parking and the preliminary stormwater pond positioned between the building and the Cameron Rd frontage. Subchapter E Section 2.2 restricts surface parking between the building and the principal street:

- **If Urban Roadway:** Parking between the building and the property line adjacent to the principal street is prohibited, except on sites 400 feet deep or less where parking may be located between the street and the building only if certain frontage build-out conditions are met (e.g., 40% of net frontage consists of continuous building facade built up to the clear zone). Even under this exception, the current layout -- where the building is fully set back behind a parking lot -- is unlikely to qualify.
- **If Suburban Roadway:** Standards are less restrictive but still require either (a) the building to be pulled up to the sidewalk/clear zone for a specified percentage of net frontage, or (b) if parking is placed in front, the site must satisfy alternative connectivity and design requirements. The Suburban Roadway classification provides the best path for the current layout but still imposes conditions.

The concept plan's layout -- building behind parking with the pond between the building and Cameron Rd -- is a classic Subchapter E conflict for auto-parts retail prototypes. AutoZone's Prototype 74 typically places the storefront facing the parking lot with the building set back, which conflicts with Subchapter E's urban-form objectives.

**Implication:** This is the single largest site plan risk. The building will likely need to be repositioned closer to Cameron Rd, with parking relocated to the side or rear. This affects the preliminary pond location, truck circulation, heritage tree CRZ zones, and the overall site geometry. Alternatively, the applicant may pursue Alternative Equivalent Compliance (AEC) to demonstrate that an alternative design meets the intent of Subchapter E without strict adherence to the parking placement and build-to zone standards.
**Next step:** (1) Confirm roadway classification. (2) Evaluate whether the prototype can be rotated/repositioned to place the building facade at the Cameron Rd frontage with parking behind or beside the building. (3) If repositioning is infeasible due to the pond, CWQZ, heritage trees, or truck-turn constraints, prepare an AEC application with supporting urban design narrative.

---

### SDUF-3: Build-to Zone / Frontage Build-Out Requirement

**Severity:** High
**Citation:** LDC 25-2, Subchapter E, Section 2.2 (Building Placement)
**Finding:** Section 2.2 requires a percentage of the net frontage along the principal street to consist of continuous building facade built up to the clear zone (or supplemental zone if provided). The required percentage varies by roadway type:

- **Urban Roadway:** Approximately 40% of net frontage must be continuous building facade at the build-to line (or higher for VMU).
- **Suburban Roadway:** A lower percentage applies, but the building must still relate to the street frontage.

The concept plan shows a 10-foot building setback from Cameron Rd, but the building is positioned in the southern/central portion of the site rather than at the Cameron Rd frontage. The Cameron Rd frontage is occupied by the driveway, preliminary pond, and open area. No portion of the building facade appears to be built to the Cameron Rd build-to zone.

**Implication:** The site plan must demonstrate that the required percentage of Cameron Rd net frontage is occupied by building facade at the build-to line. With a 7,375 SF single-story footprint (~80-90 ft wide depending on prototype dimensions), the building could potentially satisfy the frontage requirement if repositioned to face Cameron Rd. The current layout provides 0% building frontage at the build-to zone.
**Next step:** Calculate the net frontage along Cameron Rd (subtracting driveways, required landscape buffers, and easements) and determine the required build-to percentage based on the confirmed roadway classification. Evaluate whether the building footprint can meet the frontage requirement.

---

### SDUF-4: Entrance Orientation Toward Cameron Rd
